LD 718 -- An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to lssue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status

Good morning Senator Hickman and Representative Supica.
My name is Al Cleveland. I'm a resident of Portland. I am here today as the Advocacy Director of the League of Women Voters of Maine. I am testifying in opposition to 718.
The League of Women Voters of Maine is a nonpartisan political organization that has been working for
over 100 years to encourage informed and active participation in government, to increase understanding
of major public policy issues, and to influence public policy through education and advocacy. We never
support or oppose any political party or candidate.
We support ongoing absentee voting, and we oppose its repeal. Ongoing absentee voting is a
forward~thinking election policy that improves access and increases turnout wherein ballots are automatically delivered to requesting voters before every election. Participants don't need to fill out an application every time, and receiving the ballot can be a helpful reminder to the voter of an upcoming election. Voters can stay on the list as long as they are an active voter, and they can request to be removed at any time.
Ongoing absentee ballots particularly serve Maine voters who face competing Election-Day priorities and
other obstacles, including voters with limited means, bilingual households, voters with disabilities, and
voters -- often elderly citizens -- who live alone. According to the National Vote at Home Institute, 66% of
absentee voters in Maine are repeat absentee voters.
Ongoing absentee voting may also increase turnout, particularly in local and special elections, which often have drastically lower turnout. With ongoing absentee voting, the voters who have requested to
receive ballots automatically will be invited to participate in those elections by receiving a ballot in the
mail.
Across the country, ongoing absentee voting is increasingly popular. States such as Montana and Arizona have offered this service securely and successfully for well over a decade, and several states have
adopted the measure as voters have increasingly embraced absentee voting since 2020. Now is not the
time for Maine to repeal this pro-voter measure.

seems to be saying that clerks may not issue absentee ballots to voters outside their municipality, we believe this provision would be mostly meaningless. Clerks cannot now issue absentee ballots to voters outside their jurisdiction. The only time theirjurisdiction may go beyond their municipality is in the case
of unorganized townships whose elections are administered by a nearby municipality. We don't suppose
the sponsor means to suggest a reversal of that policy. But never mind that for a moment.)

We believe that third-party ballot delivery is an important service for people living in confined
circumstances, without robust mobility or transportation. Whether it's a family member, a church member, or nonpartisan volunteer, people living in communal settings may need assistance in receiving their ballots and getting them timely returned. Should a daughter in Brewer not be permitted to help her mother in assisted living in Bangor? Should a trusted friend or church volunteer from Hodgdon not be permitted to help a disabled veteran living in Houlton? If you've ever tried to provide this service, you know that the safeguards in place are rigorous. The process already requires determination. Let's not make it impossible or illegal.

Betty Martin Eliot LD 718
I support LD 718 "An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status."
As I understand it, this bill requires a municipal clerk to issue an absentee ballot only to a person who is registered to vote in that municipality, including the voter and an immediate family member or a 3rd person designated by the voter to deliver the ballot on the voter's behalf. It also repeals the provisions allowing for application for ongoing absentee voter status.
This is common sense legislation. I would assume people who weren't supposed to receive a ballot, did. Why wouldn't we want this sort of ballot restriction? Additionally, current practice allows for those age 65 or older or, who self-identifies as having a disability, can complete an application for an "ongoing absentee ballot status" to have a ballot sent to them forever. This makes zero sense. Voter status can change. People move, people die, people change parties. Who gets that ongoing supplied ballot if the voter moves or dies?
Election/voter integrity has been suspect in past elections. Why would any government/municipality be afraid of transparency? This bill, once enacted into law, would help to restore registered voters' faith in our election integrity.
Again, I support LD 718 "An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status", and it ought to pass.

RE: LD 718 An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status
Chair Hickman, Chair Supica, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs: My name is David O'Brien and I am Policy Director for RepresentUs, the nation's leading nonpartisan anti-corruption organization. RepresentUs is submitting testimony today in opposition to LD 718.
RepresentUs is a nonpartisan advocacy organization dedicated to the idea that the government should be representative of and accountable to the people. It advocates for policies to strengthen our democracy and provides activists with the resources and training to bring meaningful change.
This bill would eliminate the ability for Mainers to sign up to automatically receive absentee ballots on an ongoing basis. This would be a step backwards for Maine.
Legislation passed during the 130th Maine Legislature put into place the policy of ongoing absentee voter lists in Maine. As of November of 2023, a voter who was at least 65 years of age or who self-identified as having a disability was able to apply for status as an ongoing absentee voter. Each qualified applicant automatically received an absentee ballot for each ensuing statewide election, municipal election, and any other election for which the voter is entitled to vote and need not submit a separate request for each election. During the 131st Legislature, a bill was passed to expand the ongoing absentee status option to all Maine voters.
Eliminating this option for voters would be a mistake. Allowing voters to sign up to automatically receive absentee ballots is a way to increase efficiency, while maintaining security, in our elections system. It costs town clerks resources - time and money - to process absentee ballot requests. In addition, the majority of absentee voters in Maine choose that option in multiple elections. Data shows that 168,754 voters cast an absentee ballot in all 3 of the last even-year elections (2020, 2022 and 2024), creating duplicative work for town election officials. The

With the increased popularity of this voting option, we should be looking for ways to make it a smooth and efficient process for both voters and clerks.
Absentee voting is an important option for many groups who find it difficult to access polling places in person. Maintaining the option for voters to join an ongoing absentee voting list will ensure we continue to prioritize access to the ballot, especially for voters in rural areas, voters with disabilities, older voters, and those with inflexible work schedules, among and others who struggle to access polling places.
The practice of offering ongoing absentee voting lists is growing across the country. Seven states and the District of Columbia have on-going absentee mailing lists: Arizona, Illinois, Maryland, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, and Virginia. Re: LD 718
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and the distinguished members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee,
Mainers For Modern Elections would like to share our opposition to LD 718.
Mainers for Modern Elections is a non-partisan coalition of advocacy groups that believes a functioning democracy requires easy access to the ballot for eligible voters, especially for marginalized voting populations; strong voter protections; and confidence in a secure, modern, representative, and wellresourced elections system. The coalition advocates for statutorily protected voting rights, structural democracy reforms that expand voter access, and investment in and modernization of election administration and implementation. We pursue these policies through direct and grassroots advocacy and by educating and providing resources to public officials and coalition members.
LD 718 would take away a secure option for many Mainers to cast their ballot.It would also place undue burdens on many of Maine's citizens, especially seniors, rural voters and those with a disability. In 2024, 379,170 Maine citizens cast an absentee ballot. Of these voters over 45% were over the age of 65. Maine is the oldest state in the nation and growing older. Many older Mainers no longer drive or choose not to in the dark winter months. Getting out for basic needs, not to mention voting, can become increasingly difficult. The 129th Maine Legislature passed ongoing absentee voting with these voters and barriers in mind.
By implementing a `single sign-up' process for ongoing absentee applications, election officials see an increase in predictability for planning purposes. Data from clerks across the country and from varying sizes of offices indicate that it costs between $3.50 and $10 to process a single absentee request. Based on these numbers, it was estimated that Maine will save between $450,000 and $1.3 million simply by eliminating repetitive requests year over year. 168,754 voters cast an absentee ballot in all 3 of the last even-year elections (2020, 2022 and 2024), creating year over year duplicative work for town election officials. The secure ongoing absentee voting process was designed to reduce this redundancy and increase efficiency for town election officials.
Maine citizens of all ages can face challenges to casting their ballot, getting time off from work during polling hours, missing registration deadlines and struggling to get to their polling location. Ongoing absentee voting solves all of these problems and creates an expectation for voters that they will have a

consistent and convenient voting experience every election. Repealing this secure system that builds in efficiency for Maine citizens and our hard working town clerks before it has gone into full effect would simply be wrong.
LD 718 would also prevent town clerks from issuing absentee ballots to family members who don't live in the same jurisdiction. Citizens who are casting their ballots should be able to delegate who picks up their ballot to a trusted family member. The adult daughter who lives in Wells and cares for her elderly mother in Eliot would be prohibited from picking up her mother's absentee ballot from the Eliot town clerk. These are unnecessary burdens that do nothing to improve Maine's election process.
Mainers for Modern Elections urges you to vote ought not to pass on LD 718.
Thank you for the opportunity to submit this testimony.
Elizabeth Allen Wells, Maine

Testimony in Support of LD 718: "An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That
Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status"
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and the distinguished members of the Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs, my name is Harris Van Pate and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to testify in support of LD 718, which seeks to reinforce election integrity and streamline the absentee voting process by requiring municipal clerks to issue absentee ballots only to residents of their respective municipalities and eliminate ongoing absentee voter status.
Strengthening Election Integrity and Trust
The foundation of a secure and trustworthy electoral system is ensuring that ballots are distributed properly and only to eligible voters. Under current law, municipal clerks may distribute absentee ballots without sufficient residency verification. This creates vulnerabilities that can compromise the integrity of our elections. LD 718 provides a necessary safeguard by ensuring that clerks only issue absentee ballots to those who reside in their municipalities, reducing the risk of improper ballot distribution and fraudulent voting.
Eliminating Ongoing Absentee Voter Status
Maine's ongoing absentee voter status allows voters to automatically receive absentee ballots for every election, even if they move away from a jurisdiction. This well-intended but flawed policy increases the risk of using outdated voter rolls to send ballots to unintended recipients. LD 718 addresses this issue by eliminating ongoing absentee voter status, requiring voters to request an absentee ballot for each election in which they wish to participate. This simple change ensures that absentee ballots are issued based on up-to-date voter information while preserving voter access to absentee voting when needed.
Benefits of LD 718
- Enhances Election Security - By restricting absentee ballot issuance to municipal residents, LD 718 prevents misallocation of ballots and reduces risks associated with outdated voter rolls.

- Increases voter trust - Over half of voters believe voter fraud through absentee voting is a problem, and reducing the risk of fraud would help address those concerns.1
- Improves Administrative Efficiency - Municipal clerks will have clearer guidelines on absentee ballot issuance, reducing the number of more challenging to count and record absentee ballots as well.2
- Preserves Voter Accessibility While Reducing Risk - Voters can still request an absentee ballot for any election, ensuring broad access while preventing ballots from being automatically sent to outdated or incorrect addresses.
A Prudent Step Toward Secure Elections
LD 718 is a reasonable and necessary reform that aligns with best practices for election security while ensuring that voters retain full access to absentee voting. Maine can be a leader in election integrity by implementing policies prioritizing accuracy, accountability, and public trust.
Conclusion
Ensuring fair and transparent elections is fundamental to our democratic process. By supporting LD 718, the Legislature can take meaningful action to improve the security and administration of absentee voting while maintaining accessibility for all Maine voters. For these reasons, Maine Policy respectfully urges the committee to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 718. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Chairperson, members of the committee,
I am writing to express my strong support for LD 718. This bill would ensure that municipal clerks issue absentee ballots only to individuals registered to vote in that municipality--whether directly to the voter, an immediate family member, or a designated third party authorized by the voter. Additionally, it would repeal the provision allowing voters to apply for ongoing absentee voter status.
This legislation is a common-sense measure to safeguard election integrity. The current system raises concerns about ballots potentially being issued to individuals who are no longer eligible. Restricting absentee ballots to registered voters within the municipality they reside in helps ensure that only qualified voters participate in elections.
Furthermore, the existing provision allowing individuals aged 65 or older, or those who self-identify as having a disability, to receive an ongoing absentee ballot indefinitely is problematic. Voter status can change--people move, change political affiliations, or unfortunately pass away. Without proper oversight, ongoing absentee ballots could be sent to addresses where the intended recipient no longer resides, raising concerns about potential misuse.
Election integrity has been a growing concern in recent years. Transparency and accountability in the voting process are essential to maintaining public trust. LD 718 is a step in the right direction to reinforce confidence in our elections.
For these reasons, I urge the committee to support LD 718 and recommend its passage.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Re:

LD 718 - An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to

Residents of that Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status

Position:

OPPOSE

The Maine Town & City Clerks' Association is in strong opposition to LD 718 and we thank you for the opportunity to outline our points for your Committee.

Although ongoing absentee status is logistically more manual and cumbersome for clerks to administer, members felt that removing that option would make it more difficult for some voters to vote. Members pointed out, however, that the new CVR system should help to automate this program to make it easier to administer.

Since its inception, clerks who have administered local elections that typically see lower turnout have seen stronger turnout numbers, due to absentee ballots being returned from voters with ongoing status, many of whom may not have taken the time to request a ballot for a small local election.

All members questioned the proposed restriction on issuing absentee ballots to family members or third parties that are not residents of their municipality and wondered what problem was being solved by this. Clerks expressed concern for residents who are homebound or otherwise disabled that may be disenfranchised if their only caregiver or family member resides in another town. Members felt strongly that this will make it more difficult for some voters to cast their ballots.

The Maine Town & City Clerks' Association appreciates the opportunity to share its testimony with the Committee. Should any questions arise, please feel free to contact me at (207)680-4210 or by email: pdubois@waterville-me.gov .

10035270:
Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
In Opposition To
LD 718 - An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status March 3, 2025
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee, my name is Rebecca Lambert, and I am providing testimony in opposition to LD 718 on behalf of the Maine Municipal Association's (MMA) elected 70-member Legislative Policy Committee (LPC). For reference, the LPC guides MMA's advocacy efforts and establishes positions on bills of municipal interest.
When reviewing this bill, municipal officials are left feeling a little confused. While the merits for maintaining credibility and security in the election process are important, the approach this bill takes appears to contradict that sentiment. In fact, local leaders believe that this bill would increase barriers by making it more difficult for voters who need a third party to assist them with their absentee ballots. Restricting a voter to only use a third party located within their municipality removes their freedom to choose a person they are comfortable with to assist them with performing their constitutional right. The potential for this bill to disenfranchise voters is too great a risk for our members to support.
Additionally, municipal officials are concerned that this would make it more difficult for clerks to perform their duties as it pertains to outreach efforts in nursing homes for example. If the provisions in LD 718 were enacted, municipal clerks who work in one community but reside in another would be prohibited from conducting this important task.
Another provision of LD 718 would remove the ability for an individual to apply for ongoing absentee voter status. However, local officials believe that removing this allowance would further disenfranchise voters by further placing restrictions on the methods in which they can cast their ballot.
Thank you for your time and for considering the municipal perspective on this issue.

Testimony of Shemia Bellows, Secretary of State Department of the Secretaiy of State

Testifying against
L.D. 7l 8 "An Act to Require Municipal Clerks to Issue Absentee Ballots Only to Residents of That
Municipality and to Eliminate Ongoing Absentee Voter Status"
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans
and Legal Affairs, my name is Shenna Bellows, I live in Manchester, and I am the Secretary of State. I am speaking today against L.D. 718.
This bill would limit a voter's ability to designate an immediate family member or trusted person to deliver an absentee ballot to a person who is registered to vote in the same municipality as them. This would severely limit ballot access for older Mainers and Mainers with disabilities who rely on trusted family members, neighbors, and community members who do not happen to live within the same municipal boundaries that they do. Should a voter have to choose someone they don't know or trust to
deliver their ballot to them, just because they have the same residence municipality listed on their voter
registration? We think it is better to leave the law as is and allow voters to designate any immediate
family member or person to deliver the voter's ballot. _
Additionally, L.D. 718 would repeal ongoing absentee voting for Maine voters. Right now, Maine
voters who are 65 years and older or who self-identify as having a disability may apply for ongoing
absentee status -- and many have. We have already started to hear from municipal clerks that ongoing absentee status is increasing voter turnout in local elections - a welcome result of this law. We should
not go back on that.
Finally, this bill would remove the requirement that a voter be asked to provide their telephone number and email address, if available. This helps clerks contact a voter if their absentee ballot envelope is
missing required items, like a signature, so that their ballot may be counted. The email and phone
number are confidential and only used for ballot curing. We cannot think of a reason to want to remove
this subsection from statute.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify, and I am happy to answer any questions you may have.
